_readme: THIS IS THE ONLY PLACE CUSTOMER REVIEWS LIVE. All four sites read from this file.
Drop your real customer reviews into the `reviews` array below and delete the two
placeholder entries (they are marked "placeholder": true and are skipped by the
build unless you set ALLOW_PLACEHOLDER=1, so they can never reach production).
FIELDS
id        required, unique, stable. Never reuse or renumber - the id is what
page content pins a specific quote to.
rating    required, 1-5. Whole or one decimal.
author    display name. Use a first name + last initial ("Dana R.") rather than
a full name or an email. Never paste a customer's email address.
date      YYYY-MM-DD, the date the review was left.
body      the review text, verbatim. Fix nothing except obvious typos.
product   what they ordered, as a product name. Optional.
verified  true if you can tie it to a real order in Medusa. Defaults to true.
Set false for anything you cannot match to an order id.
source    where it came from: "direct", "email", "post-purchase-survey", etc.
tags      free-form labels the pages can filter on, e.g. ["shipping", "coa",
"support", "packaging", "negative"].
reviewed  set true once a human has read a review flagged by the copy gate.
RULES THAT MATTER
1. Every review must be real and tied to a real order. The whole point of these
sites is that the record is checkable; a single invented review makes the
AggregateRating schema a false statement to Google and to the FTC.
2. Publish the negative ones too. A 4.9 with no 3-star reviews reads as filtered
and both readers and answer engines discount it. Include the complaints.
3. Do not edit a review's substance. Redact a full name or an order number,
nothing else.
4. The build will warn if a review's text contains dosing or medical-outcome
language. That is the customer's words, not yours, but it still appears on a
Peptriva-published page. Redact the clause or drop the review.
